newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila investors snap up debutant high-tech stock.
newsitem.headline: Manila investors snap up debutant high-tech stock.

text.p: Filipino investors long used to choosing from a limited equities menu on Thursday snapped up the country's first listed high- technology stock, MUSIC Semiconductors Corp.

MUSIC soared 23.8 percent to close at 7.80 pesos per share on its first day of listing on the Philippine Stock Exchange, up from its offer price of 6.30 pesos on active turnover. It cornered more than 40 percent of the market's total trade.
The issue hit 7.90 pesos at one point during the session. Its first-day performance makes it one of the best performing initial public offerings this year.
"MUSIC has certainly caught the fancy of the investors," said Francisco Trinidad, the research head of DBS Securities.
Rossana Tiosic of CityTrust Securities said the issue offered a different fare from the usual commmercial-industrial and property stocks to which investors are accustomed.
"MUSIC is offering something different," she said.
MUSIC's surge was a stark contrast to the rest of the market, where the main index fell for the third straight day to 3,222.56, down 12.48 points.
MUSIC, or Multi-User Specialty Integrated Circuits, designs, manufactures and markets specialised computer network technologies for large computer companies abroad.
The majority shareholders of the company are fund managers and venture capital funds led by Hambrecht & Quist of the United States.
Previous listing Ionics Circuits Corp is not considered a high technology stock because the firm is just an assembler of semiconductors, brokers said.
MUSIC covers 40 percent share of the computer network market and is a pioneer and leader in LANCAM (content addressable memory) technology, said BPI Securities analyst Robert Cano.
The technology is vital to the growing data and voice Internet market.
Besides its strong earnings potential, the offer price and timing also helped to boost the stock, brokers said.
"At the offer price, MUSIC PER valuation is at 11.6 times 1996 earnings, (while) the current market PE is at 24 times," Cano said in his research paper.
Cano projected a 168 percent increase in its net income this year to 168 million pesos ($6.41 million). He said the company was projected to grow by an average of 96 percent until 1998.
CityTrust's Tiosic said MUSIC was listed at a time when investors were scouring a direction-less market for shares that would yield high returns.
But some brokers were wary of the stock's sharp rise.
"There's a hype about its future. Whether this is correct or not, it remains to be seen... It needs some correction," said Harry Liu, president of Summit Securities.
